label: Share with a join code
params: {via?: "online" (default: the open file is kept on the server in Preferences, `pref.publishServer`, and the server hands out the codes) | "local" (this app hosts it for people on the same network; no server), access?: "edit" (default) | "view" (online only: which code `code` is), server? (online: another server's address, with ?key=… when it needs its key), name? (online: the file's name there), port?, bind?: "lan" (default) | "local" (this machine only) | an IP address (local)} → the open file's session as `collab.peers` gives it: `code` is what others type to join (`collab.join {code}`, the Join field), `link` an invite link. Local: at once, the code carries the host's IPv4 address, port and secret (K7M2Q-…, 20 symbols). Online: status "connecting" first; once live `code` is the server's (K7M-2QX-9TD) and `share` is {via, access, shared, editCode, viewCode, editLink, viewLink}: links made for others (the file's own links in `published` stay yours); `code` stays null when the server is older than join codes (give `share.editLink` / `share.viewLink` instead). Called again while shared: only switches which code `code` is (`access`). Called after `collab.stop` on a file that is still on the server: new links and codes for that same file (nothing is published twice). `collab.stop` stops sharing

label: Stop live session
params: {} → {ended}: the open file's session ends (a session this app hosts stops for everyone; a joined one is left). A file shared online with `collab.share` is different: its sharing stops → {ended: false, shared: false}: the links and codes others got are revoked on the server, whoever joined with them is disconnected at once (they keep their copy), and you stay in the file, which stays on the server, open only to you (`collab.share` shares it again with new codes; `collab.leave` leaves it there; `collab.manageFile {action: "remove"}` with its owner token takes it off the server)

label: Join live session

Then: the server has everything in the copy → nothing more; the copy has changes of yours the server never confirmed and nothing else changed there → they are applied on top as one edit ("Recovered changes", synced to everyone); anything else changed meanwhile → the copy opens beside the file as “<name> (recovered copy)”; the file can't be joined → the copy opens as an unsaved document.
